stem: Tamsulosin is used to treat which urologic condition?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — BPH is tamsulosin's listed use.
options.explanation: Tamsulosin, an alpha blocker, treats benign prostatic hyperplasia, an enlarged prostate that can cause difficult, painful or frequent urination.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes any bladder-outlet complaint improves when outlet muscle relaxes.
options.explanation: Stress incontinence stems from weak urethral support; relaxing bladder-neck smooth muscle with an alpha blocker would worsen leakage, not treat it.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Confuses benign enlargement of the prostate with prostate malignancy.
options.explanation: Prostate adenocarcinoma is treated with surgery, radiation or androgen deprivation; an alpha blocker has no antitumor effect.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes any urinary symptom responds to an alpha blocker.
options.explanation: Nocturnal enuresis in children is managed with enuresis alarms or desmopressin; tamsulosin has no role in it.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Confuses infectious urinary symptoms with obstructive ones.
options.explanation: Uncomplicated bacterial cystitis is treated with antibiotics such as nitrofurantoin; tamsulosin has no antimicrobial effect.

context: Learning objective: Tamsulosin, an alpha blocker, treats benign prostatic hyperplasia, an enlarged prostate that causes urinary difficulty.
